persona: Small NJ landlord/investor (2-4 rentals across Burlington/Mercer/Middlesex), unsentimental and ROI-driven, deciding sell-now vs hold. Wants net proceeds after ALL tax, capital-gains/depreciation awareness, cap-rate and hold-vs-sell math. Financially literate, desktop, skeptical of fluff.
journey_notes: Landed expecting analytical seller tools. Tools hub surfaces 'Should I Sell Now', 'Net Proceeds Calculator', plus a home-value estimator and a buyer affordability calc.

Proceeds calculator is the strongest asset for me: it models agent commission, NJ Realty Transfer Fee (correct tiered formula in toolsCalc.ts calcNJRTF), title, attorney, misc, and mortgage payoff, and crucially has a 'Primary Residence?' toggle. Selecting No switches NJ withholding from the 2% resident GIT to 8.97% of estimated gain (salePrice - purchasePrice - commission - RTF - 3000). That single toggle is the ONLY investor-aware feature on the entire public site and it earned a moment of respect.

But the math stops exactly where an investor's analysis begins. The 8.97% is only NJ withholding. There is ZERO mention of federal capital gains (15-20%), depreciation recapture (25% — unavoidable for a rental and often the biggest line), or NIIT (3.8%). Words 'depreciation' and 'capital gains' do not appear on the proceeds page at all. As a landlord my real tax bill is dramatically understated, so the 'net proceeds' number is misleading for my use case.

'Should I Sell My House Now?' is a pure market-timing score (market type, YoY price, DOM, % over list, inventory trend). It never asks about rent roll, cap rate, cash flow, vacancy, interest rate on my note, or opportunity cost of capital. It answers 'is the market hot' but not my actual question: 'does selling beat continuing to collect rent?'. For an owner-occupant it's fine; for me it's irrelevant — it cannot model hold-vs-sell.

Home-value estimator does apply a 1.15x multiplier for multi-family (toolsCalc PROPERTY_TYPE_MULTIPLIER), and the QualificationQuiz/proceeds interest dropdown both include 'Multi-Family' and 'Investment Property' — so the system acknowledges I exist. The lead form's interest select even has 'Investment Property'.

Discovered (only by reading source, not visible to a visitor) that Steven HAS a full 5-email investor drip — investor-2-roi covers cap rate and cash flow, investor-4-tax covers 1031 exchange, depreciation, capital gains. So the investor sophistication exists, but it is entirely backend/email-gated. None of it is shown on any public page to earn my trust BEFORE I hand over contact info.

Convert-or-bounce moment: I toggled 'Primary Residence = No' in the proceeds calc, saw the result still ignore federal cap gains + depreciation recapture, and concluded the public tooling treats me as an owner-occupant. At that point the only way to get investor-grade analysis is to submit a form and hope — a leap of faith with no on-page proof. That is where I bounce or, at best, fill the form skeptically.
friction: Net proceeds for a non-primary property omit federal capital gains tax, depreciation recapture (25%), and NIIT — the largest costs for a landlord. The displayed 'what you walk away with' is materially overstated for an investor, which a financially literate user will catch and lose trust over.

No hold-vs-sell / cap-rate / rental-yield tool anywhere. 'Should I Sell Now' scores market heat only and cannot answer an investor's actual ROI question (sell proceeds reinvested vs continued cash flow + appreciation).
No multi-property or portfolio view — every tool is single-property. A 2-4 unit landlord must run each property separately with no aggregate.
Investor expertise (1031, depreciation, cap rate) is locked inside the email drip; nothing on the public pages signals 'this agent understands investors' to justify converting.

Visible polish bug undermining credibility on the exact CTA: the mid-page conversion block on BOTH tool pages reads 'See What Your Your Town Home Could Sell For' — an un-interpolated {town} placeholder ('Your Your Town'). On a numbers page, a templating error reads as sloppiness.
Exit-tax copy is resident-centric; the non-resident/investor 8.97% path is buried as a footnote-style note rather than given a tailored investor breakdown.
biggest_blocker: The seller tools are built for sentimental owner-occupants, not investors. Net-proceeds math stops at NJ withholding and ignores federal capital gains + depreciation recapture (the dominant cost for a rental), and there is no hold-vs-sell / cap-rate analysis anywhere. A skeptical, ROI-driven landlord sees shallow math, concludes the site doesn't understand investors, and bounces before the form — even though Steven actually has investor depth hidden in a backend email drip that never surfaces on-page.
score_justification: The non-primary exit-tax toggle and 'Investment Property' option earn a sliver of credit, but owner-occupant-grade math (no cap gains/recapture/cap-rate, no hold-vs-sell) and a visible 'Your Your Town' bug fail the skeptical-investor sniff test before conversion.
